title: 8. Unicode 18 changes (measured against a Unicode 17 backend)

samples.label: Question mark + virama + TA (Indic conjunct, UAX #29 GB9c)
samples.note: Unicode 18 simplified the conjunct-linker rule (UAX #29 GB9c): under mode 2027 this is ONE cluster where 17.0 made two. The advance is 2 in both releases, so width cannot see the change. Under the legacy contract the atoms stay separate in both releases. Any artwork difference depends on the fonts in use; judge it on the artwork case, not here.

samples.label: Virama + KA (conjunct linker with no preceding consonant)
samples.note: Control. UAX #29 splits this in 17.0 and joins it in 18.0, but a terminal has no cell for a leading zero-width linker: both releases were measured as one atom with an advance of 1, so the change is invisible in this position.

samples.label: Grinning face + ZWJ + U+1F7FF
samples.note: U+1F7FF was Extended_Pictographic while unassigned, so 17.0 joined it to the emoji ZWJ sequence and a cluster-capable terminal reported 2. Unicode 18 assigns it as an ordinary symbol, so the sequence breaks in two and the cluster contract is 3. A terminal still reporting 2 here is using Unicode 17 data.

samples.label: U+1FADD PICKLE, a base added in Unicode 18.0
samples.note: Width 2 under both contracts. Fonts lag new Unicode releases, so a missing-glyph box here is a font-coverage observation, not a width failure.

samples.label: U+2B81E, a Han ideograph added in Unicode 18.0
samples.note: Already Wide by block before assignment, so the advance is unchanged; what changed is Script=Han membership, which a terminal may use for font routing.
